title: Economics Cassette Series - 206 surviving tapes, 1969-1978 (SUMMARY ROW, not a single work)
notes: GAP ROW standing in for ~206 individual episodes. Biweekly subscription audio commentary tied to Friedman's Newsweek columns, produced by Instructional Dynamics (Chicago); usual interviewer William Clark (Chicago Tribune), with Rose Friedman interviewing during a six-month Vermont stay and Paul Samuelson substituting on a few programs. Hoover holds 206 of the 215-cassette set - 'apparently the definitive collection'. The tape-by-tape list (topics, plus dates and contributor names where known) was compiled by Hoover staff from cassette labels and lives in BOX 103 of the Milton Friedman papers; it was NOT retrievable online in this session, so no per-episode rows were created rather than guess at them. Most cassettes are still undigitized - Hoover digitizes on researcher request. A Carnegie Mellon catalog record dates the series 1969-1975; Hoover says 1969-78.

title: Donahue (the 'greed' exchange)
notes: The famous exchange where Phil Donahue asks whether Friedman ever doubted capitalism given 'the greed and the concentration of power' and Friedman answers 'Is there some society you know that doesn't run on greed?'. Year 1979 is agreed by multiple secondary sources (Mackinac Center, Libertarian Institute, Rush Limbaugh archive) but NO exact air date or episode number was findable; no archival host located. Widely circulated on YouTube as 'Milton Friedman on The Donahue Show - Full Interview - What is Greed?' plus a ~2-minute excerpt - URL left blank because no canonical/stable link was verified. Friedman appeared on Donahue more than once (later appearances in the 1980s are referenced but undated).

title: Episode 1: The Power of the Market
notes: Two-part hour: a documentary half filmed on location, then a studio discussion/debate half in which Friedman takes on a panel of critics (moderated discussion, recorded at the University of Chicago).
